AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to providing a New York state
residential property tax relief act for public education aid apportionment for
certain school years; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon the
expiration thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1707

SPONSOR: BROOKS
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
providing a New York state residential property tax relief act for
public education aid apportionment for certain school years; and provid-
ing for the repeal of such provisions upon the expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to provide a residential property tax relief
act for public education aid apportionment for certain school years

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. provides the title.

Section 2. provides legislative findings.

Section 3. amends Section 3602 of the education law by adding a new
subdivision 42 providing a methodology for the allocation of funds for
residential tax relief; including a tax equalization apportionment; a
tax limitation ceiling apportionment; a wealth adjusted tax rate appor-
tionment and a residential property tax levy reduction apportionment. It
also provides definitions of total property tax levy, total proposed
spending and other terms.

Section 4. makes a reference to section 3609-a of the education law
regarding the payment of the New York State residential property tax
relief for public education; makes reference to a new section 3609-I of
the education law.

Section 5. amends Section 3609 of the education law by adding a new
section 3609-i creating a prescribed payment schedule; designating offi-
cers responsible for the receipt of residential tax levy relief funds;
and specifies uses of these funds for the sole purpose of the reducing
the residential tax levy.

Section 6. 6a, 7 and 7 a. requires common school districts, union free
school districts, central school districts to report the amount of the
New York State Residential property tax relief act used to reduce the
residential tax levy as part of the property tax report card.

Section 8. is the enacting clause.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The legislature finds that the current primary and secondary education
funding systems, which is based on real property taxation, is antiquated
and creates serious disparities in educational opportunities and signif-
icant inequities with regard to distribution of the system's financial
burden.

The quality of education that children receive varies widely by
geographic region, as does the opportunity for children to participate
in extracurricular activities and for school districts to respond to the
needs associated with the changing demographic profile of the student
population.

In addition, residential property owners throughout the state receive
real property tax bills from their local school districts based on the
value of their homes, which is subject to multiple factors beyond their
control, rather than their financial ability to pay, creating serious
regional distortions in the relative cost of living.

The legislature further finds, changes in the federal tax code associ-
ated with the federal Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, will further
complicate the many concerns and shortfalls in the current funding and
distribution of aid formulas now in place. The legislature further finds
that our children should not be penalized based upon the geographic
location of their home, nor should financial support for the educational
system fall more heavily on those who are less able to bear the burden,
nor should homeowners be subject to tax penalties and fees as a result
of their educational tax payments.

Therefore, the legislature must take immediate action to provide relief
to those school districts most impacted by these disparities through the
Residential Property Tax Relief Act determined through a residential
property tax relief aid formula. This act shall be in effect for a peri-
od of three years to serve as a bridge period allowing the state legis-
lature to make a complete review of the educational programs and objec-
tives of the state of New York and development of an equitable funding
system for public education.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Shall take effect immediately and apply to school years beginning on
July 1, 2020.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1707A

SPONSOR: BROOKS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to providing a New York
state residential property tax relief act for public education aid
apportionment for certain school years; and providing for the repeal of
such provisions upon the expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to provide property tax relief to homeowners
in high-tax, low-wealth school districts for the next three years. This
bill caps the share of the school district's budget that can be paid by
property taxes and provides compensating funds from the state's general
fund.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

  Section 1. names this act the "New York state residential real proper-
ty tax relief act for public education."

  Section 2. describes the legislative findings.

  Section  3. describes the New York state residential real property tax
relief act for public education aid apportionment formula  and  eligible
school districts.

  Section  4. amends subdivision 1 of subsection 3609-a of the education
law by ensuring that the provisions of section 3609-i  is  not  paid  by
funds from the GSPS.

  Section  5. amends the education law by adding a new section 3609-i to
outline a schedule of payments for the residential property  tax  relief
act for public education aid apportionment.

  Section  6. amends paragraph a of subdivision 7 of section 1608 of the
education law by requiring the trustee or board of  trustees  to  submit
the  total tax levy reduction due to the residential property tax relief
act for public education aid apportionment into the property tax  report
card submitted annually.

  Section  7. amends paragraph a of subdivision 7 of section 1716 of the
education law by requiring the board of education to  submit  the  total
tax  levy  reduction  due to the residential property tax relief act for
public education aid apportionment into the  property  tax  report  card
submitted annually.

  Section 8. is the enacting clause.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The  current  primary  and  secondary education funding system, which is
based largely upon real property taxation,  is  antiquated  and  creates
serious  disparities  in  educational  opportunity  and  inequities with
regard to distribution of the system's financial burden. The quality  of
education  that  children receive varies widely by geographic region, as

does the opportunity for  children  to  participate  in  extracurricular
activities.

In  addition,  taxpayers  throughout the state receive real property tax
bills from their local school districts based  on  the  value  of  their
homes,  which is subject to multiple factors beyond their control rather
than their financial ability  to  pay.  This  creates  serious  regional
distortions in the relative cost of living.

The  legislature finds that these distortions are greatly exacerbated by
the recent enactment of the federal Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, which
will limit the deductibility of state and local taxes  to  ten  thousand
dollars  beginning  in  the next fiscal year. Effectively, that cap will
eliminate one of the few mitigating factors against high property  taxes
for homeowners in certain regions of the state and create undue hardship
for  families throughout the state. Our children should not be penalized
based upon the geographic location of their home, nor should the respon-
sibility to pay for the educational system fall harder on those who  are
less able to bear the burden.

This  bill  provides  tax  relief  to the families who need it most, and
importantly does not increase the state's taxing  authority.  This  bill
provides  a  formula  to fund three years of tax relief in several tiers
determined by school districts' wealth, tax burdens, and other factors.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

This bill is a revenue-neutral tax shift  and  does  not  authorize  any
additional  taxing authority. All funding for the Residential real prop-
erty tax relief act for public education will be  provided  by  existing
state resources.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This  act  shall  take  effect immediately and shall apply to the school
years commencing on and after July 1, 2021; provided that the provisions
of this act shall expire and be deemed repealed on July 1, 2024.  Effec-
tive  immediately  the  addition, amendment and/or repeal of any rule or
regulation necessary for the implementation of this act on its effective
date are authorized to be made and completed on or before such effective
date.

summary: Provides a New York state residential property tax relief act for public education aid apportionment for certain school years; and provides for the repeal of such provisions upon the expiration thereof.
